title: Shift compatibility of strict-system realization maps
statement: Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$. Let $W$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme with its small pro-etale site, put $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$, and let $\mathscr S_W$ be the abelian category of strict semilinear systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves with derived reduction $\mathcal R_W$ and total-limit functor $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$. Restrict to normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude in common finite intervals. For a finite well-typed expression $V$ in the system pullback, system direct image, open extension and derived tensor, with derived-complete constructible integral inputs $K_1,\ldots,K_s$ and all intermediate objects in those bounds, let $c_V:\mathcal L_WV(\mathcal R K_1,\ldots,\mathcal R K_s)\xrightarrow{\sim}V_{\mathrm{int}}(K_1,\ldots,K_s)$ be the canonical realization isomorphism of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Treat input slots as individual leaf occurrences in the expression tree; a repeated object has independent occurrence slots. For a designated input slot $i$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$, write $V^{(i,r)}$ for the same expression with only $K_i$ replaced by $K_i[r]$; for a tensor node, the comparison in the shifted slot is the signed tensor comparison (in particular this specifies the second-slot Koszul sign). For each compactification $f=pj$, choose the strict tower model $U_W S_pJ_j\mathcal R K$ (termwise restriction of scalars of a simultaneous system resolution) realizing the inverse system in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and use its Roos total-cone representative, and define the completed integral shift on $Rf_!$ by the termwise cochain shift and the induced shifted-cone comparison of that representative. Equip the system expression and its integral counterpart with these slotwise canonical shift comparisons. Then for every $i,r$, the square expressing that $c_{V^{(i,r)}}$ after the system shift equals the integral shift after $c_V$ commutes, naturally in all inputs. The same holds after whiskering by any such expression and for every canonical system map (units, counits, pullback/tensor maps, direct-image compositors, proper/open interchange and projection maps) together with its corresponding integral map.

source.place: Unit Step 2 (the adic stage): the normalized strict-system construction and its transport to the integral derived category

proof.text: Write $\chi_H:H(M[r])\to H(M)[r]$ for a comparison in one designated input occurrence, with all others fixed. The basic-operation statement supplies the natural, coherent comparisons on $P_v,S_p,J_j,\otimes^L$, their integral counterparts, and $d_A$; it specifies the signed second tensor slot. The reduction/total-limit statement supplies those on $\mathcal R,\mathcal L$ and the actual $u,e$. Use the K-injective strict-tower Roos model of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] for $\mathcal L$. Its derived products and $1-s$ are functorial on strict tower maps; the shifted-cone comparison fixes the sign. This specifies every shift comparison used below; no tensor/pullback lemma without a shift clause is being cited for one.

source.place: Maps-used and coefficient-comparison sentences: fix the operation and total-limit shift structures; agent-written shift calculation

proof.text:
Use the recursive-characterization statement [lem-pur-integral-realization-recursion], not formulas extracted without citation from a proof of the realization theorem. It states for the actual canonical comparisons that $c_{K_i}=u_{K_i}^{-1}$,
$$a_A(M)=d_A(\mathcal LM)(\mathcal LA(e_M))^{-1},\qquad a_\otimes(M,N)=d_\otimes(\mathcal LM,\mathcal LN)(\mathcal L(e_M\otimes^Le_N))^{-1},$$
and
$$c_{AV}=A_{\rm int}(c_V)a_A(M),\qquad c_{V\otimes T}=(c_V\widehat\otimes^Lc_T)a_\otimes(M,N).$$
Here $M=V(\mathcal RK_i)$, $N=T(\mathcal RK_i)$; $u,e$ are invertible on the complete/normalized domains. The $d_A$ are exactly those specified by [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence]. Thus we prove a property of the given $c_V$, rather than choosing a different family. The induction claim for a tree $V$ is $\chi_{V_{\rm int}}c_{V^{(i,r)}}=c_V[r]\chi_{\mathcal LV\mathcal R}$ for each of its independent leaf slots.

source.place: Coefficient-comparison construction: expose the canonical recursion and state the induction claim; agent-written shift calculation

proof.text: The unit square from [lem-pur-reduction-limit-shift-adjunction] gives the induction base for $c_{K_i}=u_{K_i}^{-1}$ by multiplying that square by the inverse units. For $a_A$, the square for $e_M$ remains a square after applying $\mathcal LA$, by composition/whiskering [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker]. The square for $d_A$ and naturality in $\mathcal LM$ give a square for $d_A(\mathcal LM)$. An invertible square remains commutative on inverting its horizontal maps: from $s_2h'=h[r]s_1$ one obtains $s_1(h')^{-1}=h[r]^{-1}s_2$. Composing these two squares gives the square for $a_A$. For $a_\otimes$, apply this argument to $e_M\otimes1$ and $1\otimes e_N$ separately and use bifunctoriality; the signed comparisons and naturality are part of the basic-operation statement.

source.place: Coefficient-comparison sentence: shift squares of the adjunction insertions; agent-written shift calculation

proof.text:
Suppose the induction claim holds for $V$ and put $M=V(\mathcal RK_i)$. Applying $A_{\rm int}$ to that square gives the square for $A_{\rm int}(c_V)$ with the composite comparisons: this is precisely whiskering clause (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker], using the natural shift comparison of the integral operation supplied by [lem-pur-integral-basic-operation-shift]. In formulas, with the inner comparison denoted $s$, the equation is
$$\chi_{A_{\rm int}V_{\rm int}}\,A_{\rm int}(c_{V^{(i,r)}})=A_{\rm int}(c_V)[r]\,\chi_{A_{\rm int}\mathcal LV\mathcal R}.$$
Paste this with the square for $a_A(M)$ in step 3 and substitute $c_{AV}=A_{\rm int}(c_V)a_A(M)$ from [lem-pur-integral-realization-recursion]. The middle comparisons cancel, yielding the induction claim for $AV$. Every invocation decreases the number of tree nodes.

source.place: Coefficient-comparison sentence: unary expression-tree induction; agent-written shift calculation

proof.text: At a tensor node the designated occurrence lies in exactly one of the two independent leaf sets. If it lies in $V$, tensor its induction square with $c_T$ and use naturality of the completed tensor comparison in the other factor; if it lies in $T$, do the same with $c_V$ fixed. Paste with the corresponding slot square for $a_\otimes$ from step 3. The tensor recursion of [lem-pur-integral-realization-recursion] then gives the claim for $V\otimes T$. In the second case the comparison is the signed one of [lem-pur-integral-basic-operation-shift]; it is not the unsigned identification of graded objects. These unary and binary cases exhaust the finite tree. All intermediate systems remain in the explicitly assumed normalized and bounded domains; an integer shift translates a finite interval to a finite interval.

source.place: Coefficient-comparison sentence: binary expression-tree induction; agent-written shift calculation

proof.text: For system structural maps start with the primitive squares of [lem-pur-system-primitive-comparison-shift], covering pullback compositors, pullback/tensor comparisons, tensor reassociation/unit/symmetry, open composition and the specified restriction/clopen maps. For $P_v\dashv S_v$ use [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift] on the small ringed diagram topoi whose module categories realize $\mathscr S$; these are the canonical derived inverse/direct-image adjunctions of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. For $J_j\dashv P_j$ use [lem-pur-open-adjunction-shift], and for $\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L$ use [lem-pur-reduction-limit-shift-adjunction]. Thus their units and counits have shift squares before evaluation. More generally an adjunct of $h:FX\to Y$ is $G(h)\eta_X$, and a mate of $\alpha:F_2H\to TF_1$ is $G_2(T\varepsilon_1)G_2(\alpha G_1)\eta_2HG_1$. Every factor has a shift square when $\alpha$ does; composition/whiskering pastes them. In particular the direct-image compositors, conjugate to pullback compositors by the realization statement, have shift squares. This is an explicit finite-composite argument, not an assumption that mates automatically preserve the chosen shifts.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: system primitives and the three actual adjunctions; agent-written shift calculation

proof.text: Let $\beta:P_gJ_j\cong J_{j'}P_{g_U}$ and $\gamma:J_jM\otimes^LN\cong J_j(M\otimes^LP_jN)$ be the open maps of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], whose statement also applies to the ringed diagram topoi of systems. Its normalization specifies $\beta^{-1}$ as the open adjunct of $P_{g_U}u_M$ followed by the inverse pullback compositor, and $\gamma^{-1}$ as the open adjunct of $u_M\otimes1$ under restriction/tensor comparison. Here $u_M:M\to P_jJ_jM$ is the open unit, not the reduction unit. The unit squares are [lem-pur-open-adjunction-shift]; the compositor and tensor squares are [lem-pur-system-primitive-comparison-shift]. Applying the adjunct formula in step 6 proves the shift square for each inverse map, in either tensor input. Inverting those squares proves it for $\beta,\gamma$. Hence the actual normalized open maps are covered, rather than maps chosen by checking their finite evaluations.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: open base-change and open tensor normalization; agent-written shift calculation

proof.text:
For the proper/open square $Q$ of [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting], its hypotheses are exactly the proper vertical arrows and quasi-compact open horizontal arrows in the realization statement. In its notation
$$\lambda_Q:P_iS_pJ_k\cong S_qP_bJ_k\cong S_qJ_s\cong S_qS_s\cong S_r.$$
The first arrow is conjugate to the normalized cartesian open comparison, so its square follows from steps 6-7. The next two arrows use $P_bJ_k\cong J_s$ and $J_s\cong S_s$ for the clopen $s$, covered by [lem-pur-system-primitive-comparison-shift]. The last is the direct-image compositor from step 6. Pasting gives the square for this specified $\lambda_Q$. The same proper/open statement identifies $\Gamma_Q$ as the open adjunct of $\lambda_Q^{-1}$; explicitly
$$\Gamma_Q=S_pJ_k\varepsilon_r\circ S_p\alpha_QS_r\circ\eta_pJ_iS_r,\quad \alpha_Q=(J_bJ_sP_sP_q\cong J_kP_r)\circ J_b\pi_sP_q\circ\beta_{i,p}.$$
The normalized $\beta$, clopen projection $\pi_s$, compositors and proper units/counits all have the squares already established. This displayed factorization proves the square for $\Gamma_Q$ by pasting in the semilinear derived category. It also handles noncartesian refinement squares allowed by the cited statement.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: intrinsic open restriction and proper/open mate; agent-written shift calculation

proof.text:
The realization statement specifies system exchange and projection maps by the composites of [def-exchange-projection]. In system notation their factors are
$$\operatorname{Ex}_*=S_{f'}P_{g'}\varepsilon_f\circ S_{f'}\theta S_f\circ\eta_{f'}P_gS_f,\qquad \pi_{p;M,N}=S_p((\varepsilon_{p,M}\otimes1)\mu_p)\circ\eta_{p,S_pM\otimes N}.$$
The compact-support exchange is $S_{p'}\beta\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p}J_j$; the compact-support projection is $S_p\gamma\circ\pi_{p;J_jM,N}$, with the pullback compositor inserted in $\gamma$ as in the definition. Each displayed factor is a primitive square, an adjunction square or a normalized open square from steps 6-7. Composition/whiskering therefore proves these four shift equations, separately in each projection input. The proper/open squares from step 8 and direct-image/open compositors give all compactification composition and refinement maps by the same finite pasting. This uses the stated system composite formulas, not a finite-coefficient theorem applied to an integral coefficient ring.

source.place: Maps-used sentence: write the projection and exchange composites; agent-written shift calculation

proof.text:
Any allowed system map $\tau:V\to T$, including an allowed expression context around a generator, is a composite and whiskering of the preceding maps. Clause (ii)/(iii) and composition in [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] give its shift square. For a tensor context fix the other input and apply that clause; for several changing occurrences factor into single-slot maps by bifunctoriality. The realization statement gives the actual intertwining equation
$$\tau_{\rm int}=c_T\,\mathcal L(\tau)\,c_V^{-1}.$$
Both $c$ squares were proved by tree induction and $\mathcal L$ has its fixed comparison. Paste their squares with the square for $\mathcal L(\tau)$, using the inverse-square identity in step 3. The result is exactly the shift square for the corresponding integral map, together with the compatible realization square. No equality is detected after evaluating systems: all equations used here hold before evaluation.

source.place: Coefficient-comparison sentence: conjugation by the given realization maps and arbitrary contexts; agent-written shift calculation

proof.text: For $f=pj$ take a K-flat strict reduction model for $\mathcal RK$ and simultaneous direct-image/open models. Their termwise scalar restriction $U_WS_pJ_j\mathcal RK$ is the strict tower chosen in the statement. The restriction-of-scalars comparison of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] identifies its transition from $m$ to $n$ with $Rp_{*,m}j_!$ of the reduction map followed by the coefficient-restriction isomorphism. These are exactly the transitions written in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. The realization statement identifies $c_{S_pJ_j}$ with this integral compact-support functor, including its maps. Use the natural total-limit Roos model [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] of this strict tower, not a cone assigned to an incoherent diagram of objects in a derived category. Its termwise shift and shifted-cone comparison define the completed integral shift fixed in the statement. Consequently the already proved case $V=S_pJ_j$ is the required compact-support square for that model. The identity shift, positive iterations and inverse comparisons for negative integers give the same equations for every $r\in\mathbf Z$.
